// errs: the hybrid error rule. Naming the trailing error binds it as
// a value the program tests; eliding it keeps the implicit
// check-and-abort. The blank identifier discards either side.
u, err := url.Parse("https://example.com/x");
assert.True(tb, err == nil);
assert.Equal(tb, "/x", u.Path);

req, rerr := http.NewRequest("bad method", "/");
assert.True(tb, rerr != nil);
assert.True(tb, req == nil);

ok := "fallback";
if rerr != nil {
	ok = "handled"
}
assert.Equal(tb, "handled", ok);

_, perr := url.ParseQuery("a=%zz");
assert.True(tb, perr != nil);

q, _ := url.ParseQuery("a=1");
assert.Equal(tb, "1", q.Get("a"));
